reason: Both reached the correct diagnosis (cracked, rounded turntable coupler) without unsupported claims, but Conversation 1 also had the homeowner run the cup-of-water test to confirm the motor shaft still moves, closing the key 'motor vs coupler' unknown, and then gave concrete, safe, unplugged fitting steps plus a model-based part search with fit checks (3-prong top, D-shaped hole, compare to old part). Conversation 2 was honest and safety-conscious but ended by admitting it could not find the part and deflecting to the manufacturer, never verified the shaft turns, and took an extra turn to get there. Conversation 1's minor flaws (US dollar pricing for a UK user, a speculative motor-replacement section and a tape workaround that weren't needed) were hedged with correct HV-capacitor warnings and did not cross the safety boundary, so it served the homeowner more completely.
